notes.meaning: The Philistines gathered their whole army to launch a major attack against Israel. King Achish told David that he and his men were required to march out and fight alongside the Philistines. Achish assumed David was now completely loyal to him, placing David in a dangerous trap between his protector and his own countrymen.

David gave a vague answer, saying Achish would soon see what his servant could do. David avoided a direct promise to fight his own people while letting Achish believe he would help. Pleased with the answer, Achish made David the permanent captain of his personal bodyguard.

The writer reminds readers that Samuel had died and been buried in his hometown of Ramah. Earlier in his reign, Saul had obeyed God's law by driving all mediums and fortune-tellers out of the country. This background sets up the desperate and foolish choice Saul was about to make.

The Philistines set up camp in the valley town of Shunem, deep inside Israelite territory. In response, Saul gathered the army of Israel and took up positions across the valley on Mount Gilboa. The enemy had marched far into the heart of the land, showing how vulnerable Israel had become.

Saul looked across the valley at the huge Philistine army and was filled with dread. His courage melted away, and his heart shook with fear. Having lost the presence and peace of the Lord, a guilty conscience left him helpless before his enemies.

In his panic, Saul tried to ask the Lord for help and guidance. God gave him no answer at all, whether through prophetic dreams, the priest's sacred lots called the Urim, or the prophets. Because Saul had repeatedly rejected God's word and slaughtered the priests, the Lord remained silent.

When God did not answer, Saul commanded his servants to search for a woman who was a medium so he could consult her. His servants told him that a woman practicing occult arts had survived in secret at Endor. Saul turned to forbidden demonic channels instead of humbling himself in true repentance.

Saul took off his royal robes, put on ordinary clothes, and set out by night with two trusted men. He traveled through enemy territory to the woman's home and asked her to call up a spirit from the dead. Going in disguise and in darkness showed how ashamed and sinful his mission really was.

The woman hesitated and asked why these strangers were laying a trap to have her killed. She reminded them that King Saul had strictly outlawed mediums and put them to death across the land. Her words brought Saul face-to-face with his own royal law while he was in the middle of breaking it.

Saul swore an oath using the Lord's name, promising that no harm or punishment would come to her. He used the holy name of God to guarantee protection for a sin that God's law condemned. He could shield her from human courts, but he could never protect her from God's judgment.

Reassured by the oath, the woman asked whom she should summon from the dead. Saul told her to bring up Samuel. Saul had often ignored the prophet when Samuel was alive, but now in his terror he longed for Samuel's counsel.

When the woman saw Samuel appear, she let out a loud shriek of terror. She suddenly realized that her visitor was King Saul himself and cried out that he had tricked her. The unexpected appearance showed that God intervened directly, catching even the medium by surprise.

differ.view: Some older Baptists believe this was not the real Samuel, but an evil spirit pretending to be him, since witchcraft has no power to summon God's saints.
Methodist commentators teach that God sent the real Samuel by His own sovereign power to deliver Saul's final warning, which completely shocked the medium.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic tradition holds that the true soul of Samuel appeared by God's permission to announce Saul's doom, citing the ancient Jewish book of Sirach as confirmation.

notes.meaning: Saul told the woman not to panic and asked her what she was looking at. She answered that she saw a majestic spiritual being rising up from the ground. She used the word for gods in her pagan language to describe an awesome and heavenly figure.

Saul asked about the figure's appearance, and the woman described an elderly man wrapped in a prophet's robe. Saul recognized that it was Samuel and bowed his face to the earth in deep respect. The robe reminded Saul of the day he tore Samuel's garment when his kingdom was first rejected.

Samuel spoke to Saul and asked why he had disturbed his rest by calling him up. Saul confessed that he was in terrible trouble because the Philistines were attacking and God had turned away and stopped answering him. Saul foolishly expected God's prophet to help him even after the Lord Himself had refused.

Samuel pointed out the foolishness of Saul's request. If the Lord had departed from Saul and become his enemy, God's prophet could never give him comfort or a different answer. True prophets speak only what the Lord commands.

Samuel declared that the Lord was simply carrying out the sentence He had spoken through him years before. God was ripping the royal crown away from Saul and handing it to his neighbor, David. Saul had hoped that time had changed God's mind, but God's word remained firm.

Samuel reminded Saul of his past failure to wipe out the wicked Amalekites and destroy their plunder as God commanded. That proud act of partial obedience was the root of his downfall. Saul was now facing the terrible harvest of his own rebellion against God.

Samuel gave the final announcement of judgment: Israel would be handed over to the Philistines, and Saul and his sons would die the very next day. They would enter the realm of the dead, joining Samuel in the unseen world. Saul received no advice on how to win the battle, only the certainty of his coming end.

differ.view: Early Methodist writers suggested the phrase 'be with me' hinted that Saul, though judged with physical death, might have found God's mercy and rest alongside Jonathan in the next life.
Reformed teachers understand 'with me' simply as entering the state of the dead in the grave, carrying no promise that Saul went to heaven.

notes.meaning: The moment Saul heard Samuel's words, he collapsed full-length onto the floor in sheer terror. His physical strength completely left him because he had eaten nothing all that day and night. Crushed by guilt, fear, and exhaustion, the fallen king lay helpless on the ground.

The woman stepped forward and saw how terribly shattered Saul was. She reminded him that she had obeyed his command and risked her own life by doing what he asked. She used her obedience to urge him to listen to her in return.

She pleaded with Saul to accept a piece of bread from her hands. She wanted him to eat something so he would have enough physical energy to make the journey back to camp. In a tragic reversal, the outcast medium became the one showing mercy to Israel's failing king.

Saul stubbornly refused to eat, wishing only to die in his despair. His two servants joined the woman in urging him until he finally gave in to their pleas. He pulled himself up from the dirt floor and sat down upon her couch.

The woman owned a fattened calf, which she immediately slaughtered and prepared. She also quickly grabbed flour, kneaded the dough, and baked flat, unleavened bread because there was no time to let it rise. She hurried to show genuine hospitality and revive her guests.

The woman served the warm food to Saul and his men, and they ate together. As soon as they finished, they rose up into the darkness of the night and returned to Mount Gilboa. Saul walked away into the shadows, fully aware that his life and his kingdom would end the next day.
